newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's ACES gets help from Morgan Grenfell.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's ACES gets help from Morgan Grenfell.

text.p: Colombia's second largest airline Aerolineas Centrales de Colombia (ACES) has chosen a consortium headed by investment bank Deutsche Morgan Grenfell to advise it in its search for a new partner, the company said Wednesday.

ACES, which flies domestic and international routes, announced earlier this month that current shareholders were to inject $15 million into the airline and then look for a buyer for a 30 percent stake in the company.

The ACES statement said it had signed up the Deutsche Morgan Grenfell-Avmark Inc consortium to find the best potential partner to help it "strengthen its performance in the domestic and international market ... and permit its consolidation".
The main ACES shareholder is the Grupo Cafetero conglomerate, headed by the National Coffee Growers' Federation.

ACES, which is not registered on the stock market, reported 1996 net profits of 5.3 billion pesos compared to net profits of 1.4 billion pesos in 1995. The company was Colombia's fastest growing airline in 1996 with a 13.4 percent increase in the number of passengers compared to the previous year.
